entities.name: Psammetichus IV
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Psammetichus IV or Psamtik IV is a proposed ancient Egyptian ruler who lived during the First Persian Period.

He was likely of Greek descent, possibly from the city of Halicarnassus in modern-day Turkey, and served as satrap (governor) under the Achaemenid Empire.

Psammetichus IV's reign is notable for his efforts to promote Egyptian culture and identity, as well as his military campaigns against the Nubians and the Assyrians.

Despite his significance in ancient Egyptian history, Psammetichus IV remains a somewhat controversial figure due to the limited archaeological evidence available about his life and reign.

'Egypt was more than just a kingdom; it was an heirarchy of kingdoms.' - Psammuthes, the scribe who wrote on the wall of the temple of Thoth at Hermopolis.
